problems.title: Equal arcs determine a radius ratio
problems.question: A 60° arc of circle 1 equals a 45° arc of circle 2. Find the area ratio of an equilateral triangle inscribed in circle 1 to a square inscribed in circle 2.
problems.idea: Arc length is proportional to radius times angle.
steps: Divide the two area formulas to get (3√3/8)(R₁/R₂)².
Substitute (3/4)²=9/16.

problems.title: Two possible seating arrangements
problems.question: A hall has 600 seats. Adding 4 seats to every row and 2 rows gives 748 seats. How many rows are there now?
problems.idea: Let r be the old row count.
steps: Multiply by r and simplify to r²-35r+300=0=(r-15)(r-20).
Both old counts work: 15 rows of 40 seats or 20 rows of 30 seats.
The new counts are respectively 17 rows of 44 or 22 rows of 34; both total 748.
problems.note: The data allow two distinct integer seating arrangements; neither answer can be discarded.

problems.title: Add reciprocals before inverting
problems.question: Simplify [(x√y-y√x)⁻¹+(x√y+y√x)⁻¹]⁻¹ divided by (x-y)/2.
steps: The reciprocal sum is 2x√y/[xy(x-y)]=2/[√y(x-y)].
Its reciprocal is √y(x-y)/2.
Divide by (x-y)/2 to obtain √y. The original expression requires x>0,y>0,x≠y.

problems.title: Retain the squared denominator’s sign
problems.question: Solve (x-2)/(x²-2x+1)≥x/(x²+x-2).
problems.idea: Bring the fractions to a common denominator.
steps: The squared factor is positive on the domain.
Thus the sign is that of (x-4)/(x+2), nonnegative to the left of -2 or from 4 onward.
Exclude -2 and include 4.

problems.title: A centroid triangle and Heron’s formula
problems.question: Two triangle medians have lengths 9,12 cm; the side joining their starting vertices is 7 cm. Find the triangle area.
problems.idea: The centroid reduces each median to two thirds.
steps: For triangle AGB, s=(6+8+7)/2=21/2.
Triangle AGB has one third of the full triangle’s area, so multiply by 3.

problems.title: Infinitely nested equilateral triangles
problems.question: Start with an equilateral triangle of side 6 cm. Inscribe its circle, then another equilateral triangle, and repeat. Sum all triangle perimeters.
problems.idea: Each new circumradius equals the previous inradius.
formulas: For an equilateral triangle r=R/2; S∞=first/(1-ratio).
steps: Every new side and perimeter is half the previous one.
The first perimeter is 18 cm.
The sum is 18/(1-1/2)=36 cm.

problems.title: Arithmetic first differences
problems.question: The differences bₙ₊₁-bₙ form an arithmetic progression. Given b₁=2,b₂=5,b₃=10, find b₂₀₁.
problems.idea: The differences begin 3,5 and increase by 2.
steps: Sum the first n-1 differences: (n-1)n+(n-1).
Adding 2 gives n²+1.

problems.title: Increase throughout a closed interval
problems.question: Find all a for which y=ax²-(a-2)x+3 is increasing on [-1,4].
problems.idea: Its derivative is linear, so check its minimum at an endpoint.
steps: For a≥0, the minimum derivative is at x=-1: 2-3a≥0, giving 0≤a≤2/3.
For a<0, it is at x=4: 7a+2≥0, giving -2/7≤a<0.
The endpoint cases still give a strictly increasing function: a derivative can vanish at an endpoint without a flat interval.
problems.note: The wording suggests one parameter value, but an entire interval satisfies the condition.

problems.title: An odd rational function needs a symmetric domain
problems.question: Find all a making f(x)=(ax-2)/(a²+a+x) odd.
problems.idea: The excluded input must be symmetric about zero.
steps: A domain missing only one point is symmetric only if that point is 0. Thus a=0 or a=-1.
For a=0, f(x)=-2/x is odd.
For a=-1, f(x)=-1-2/x is not odd.

problems.title: A perimeter bound that is not attained
problems.question: Given |a-b|=2 and |a+b|=4, find the smallest perimeter of the parallelogram on a,b.
problems.idea: Check whether equality would collapse the parallelogram.
steps: Adding and subtracting the squared conditions gives the two displayed identities.
Cauchy’s inequality gives |a||b|≥3, so (|a|+|b|)²=10+2|a||b|≥16. Hence P≥8.
Equality requires a,b parallel in the same direction, with lengths 3 and 1. This makes a degenerate parallelogram.
For a genuine parallelogram P>8, and values approach 8 as the vectors become parallel.
problems.answer: For a nondegenerate parallelogram there is no attained minimum; the infimum is 8. If degenerate figures are allowed, the minimum is 8.
problems.note: The often intended answer 8 is attained only by a collapsed figure. The distinction matters because the question asks for a minimum.
